cases.name: small-crud
cases.prompt: Design an internal CRUD app for 20 staff; indexed queries meet 300 ms and changes must be immediately visible.
expected: Keeps simple synchronous baseline
No speculative queue/cache/replicas/gateway
Preserves transactional invariants and required recovery

cases.name: durable-video
cases.prompt: Video jobs take 30–180 seconds. Acknowledge quickly; accepted work must survive restarts. Large media; existing PostgreSQL; traffic unknown.
expected: Async jobs, durable buffering, worker and object storage justified
Considers DB queue without requiring broker
No invented capacity facts
Covers duplicate and object/DB crash boundaries

cases.name: immediate-slow
cases.prompt: Every caller requires a finished result within 200 ms. Processing takes at least 30 seconds. Can a queue solve this?
expected: Identifies infeasible deadline
Does not silently change completion semantics
Surfaces product or computation change

cases.name: dual-write
cases.prompt: An order commits then the process crashes before publishing its required event. What mechanism is justified?
expected: Atomic state and publication intent with relay or equivalent
Acknowledges eventual publication and possible duplicates
No end-to-end exactly-once claim

cases.name: payment-timeout
cases.prompt: A payment provider times out. It may have charged the customer. We have a queue with three retries. Design recovery.
expected: Unknown outcome distinguished from failure
Provider operation identity/status or reconciliation before repeat charge
No claim local dedup makes provider effect atomic

cases.name: overload
cases.prompt: Arrivals stay at 100 jobs/s. Ten parallel workers each average one second/job. Should we add a queue?
expected: Computes nominal 10 jobs/s capacity and 90 jobs/s backlog growth
Queue cannot stabilize sustained overload
Considers bottleneck, capacity, admission and deadline

cases.name: fanout
cases.prompt: Billing, analytics and notifications must independently react to completed purchases, with independent downtime and replay.
expected: Distinguishes event subscriptions from competing workers
Defines durability, replay and duplicate effects per consumer
Does not select Kafka merely from consumer count

cases.name: stale-cache
cases.prompt: Reads are expensive, but every authorization decision must reflect revocation immediately. Should we cache everything?
expected: Does not assume stale authorization acceptable
Separates cacheable data from strict consistency path
Evaluates optimization before cache/replica

cases.name: scheduled-replay
cases.prompt: A daily settlement job spans a daylight-saving transition, may overlap, and can be manually rerun.
expected: Defines business date/timezone and missed-run policy
Distinguishes accidental duplicate from intentional rerun
Handles concurrency and irreversible effects

cases.name: scope-boundary
cases.prompt: Change the button color to blue.
expected: Does not initiate architecture analysis
